text:
alice: Ran a focused bakeoff today: SmoothQuant + AWQ vs GPTQ on long-context workloads (8k and 32k). Models: Llama-2-13b, Orca-7b. Short summary: SQ+AWQ keeps accuracy much better at 32k; GPTQ shows a ~3+ point MRR/EM degradation on our long-pass tests. Full notes & configs below.

ben: Nice — can you drop the exact configs and eval commands so I can reproduce?

alice: Yep. Repro command I used (conda env: riff-quant):
```bash
python eval_longctx.py \
  --model checkpoints/llama2-13b/float32 \
  --quant awq \
  --smoothquant true \
  --context_length 32768 \
  --batch 2 \
  --dataset longbench_passages \
  --metrics ppl,mrr,exact_match \
  --seed 42
```

carol: Config snippet for AWQ+SmoothQuant (the code toggles activation scaling pre-quant):
```ini
[quantization]
method = AWQ
bitwidth = 8
smoothquant_enable = true
smoothquant_alpha = 0.5   # activation scaling factor (0..1)
per_channel = true
clip_activations = true
clip_threshold = 0.995
```

alice: Raw numbers (shortened):
```
Model           Context   Setup         PPL   MRR    ExactMatch
llama2-13b      8k        fp32         12.3  0.742   68.1
llama2-13b      8k        GPTQ-8        12.8  0.735   67.4
llama2-13b      8k        AWQ+SQ-8      12.5  0.740   67.9
llama2-13b     32k        fp32         12.9  0.736   67.6
llama2-13b     32k        GPTQ-8       15.2  0.704   63.8   <-- big drop
llama2-13b     32k        AWQ+SQ-8     13.1  0.730   67.0

orca-7b         32k        GPTQ-8       18.4  0.612   56.2
orca-7b         32k        AWQ+SQ-8     16.1  0.643   59.9
```

eva: Interesting. Did you try varying smoothquant_alpha? Activation-aware scaling can be sensitive.

alice: Yes — quick sweep: alpha=0.3/0.5/0.8 on llama2-13b@32k:
- 0.3: slightly underfits, +0.4 MRR vs GPTQ but higher PPL on some seqs.
- 0.5: best overall tradeoff (used above).
- 0.8: too aggressive scaling, small latency hit and no extra accuracy.

carol: Also tried per-channel vs per-tensor AWQ: per-channel is noticeably better for long-range tokens (reduces kv-scale drift).

ben: What about runtime/latency for production routing? We need numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted.

alice: Measured on a 4xA100 pool: (32k context, batch1)
- FP32: 1.9s/token first pass (kv warmup) then ~0.09s/token
- GPTQ-8: 1.4s/token first pass, ~0.06s/token (but accuracy loss)
- AWQ+SQ-8: 1.55s/token first pass, ~0.065s/token (best accuracy/latency mix)
Notes: prefix KV cache warmups dominate for 32k. AWQ adds ~8-12% overhead vs GPTQ but recovers accuracy.

dev-bot: CI: quant_bakeoff/171900 took 1h22m, job passed, artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-quant/artifacts/1719008245/ :thumbsup:

eva: For deployment profiles I'd propose:
- Default route: GPTQ-8 for <=8k (best perf/cost).
- Longctx (>8k): AWQ+SQ-8 on Dedicated or Private nodes with higher mem and IO.
- Fallback: if AWQ capacity saturated, route to fp32 on Dedicated for critical requests.

carol: Agree. Also add a gating eval: run daily longbench_kv integrity check to detect drift/regressions when model or quant code changes.

ben: Any known failure modes? Long-tail sequences where AWQ still fails?

alice: Yes — some synthetic pathological repeats cause AWQ to slightly hallucinate more than fp32 (low-frequency tokens with heavy activation scaling). We flagged it in issue #1423. Short term: clip_threshold tweak + per-layer alpha schedule helps.

eva: Ok sounds actionable. Next steps?

alice: I'll open a PR with the config and add the per-layer alpha sweep to the eval harness. Plan to run 2-week stability pass across customer longctx traces.

ben: Thanks — ping me when the PR is up, I'll help with infra for dedicated routing tests. :rocket:

carol: tagging ops for capacity planning: @ops-team please note potential Dedicated pool for longctx AWQ traffic. :thinking_face:

alice: thanks all — uploaded full logs + model diffs to the ticket. We'll iterate on alpha and clip settings this week. :party:
